title: For fixed positive Poincare ranks and uniformly separated diagonal leading matrices, sufficiently small lower Laurent coefficients make Liouvillian solvability equivalent to constant simultaneous triangularization
author: Moulay A. Barkatou; Renat R. Gontsov
source_title: Linear Differential Systems with Small Coefficients: Various Types of Solvability and their Verification
difficulty_reason: The difficult step is to bound formal exponents at irregular singularities from the raw Laurent coefficients, which need not equal the residue eigenvalues. The author constructs the formal diagonalization recurrence and controls its nonlinear accumulated terms by explicit polynomial majorants depending on the spectral gap and fixed Poincare rank. This bridges local irregular asymptotics to the global differential-Galois triangularization criterion, rather than applying that criterion without verifying its exponent hypothesis.

proof_review.note: The complete new Section3 proof was read with the rational-system and generic-singularity definitions. The author explicitly constructs the formal diagonalizing gauge coefficient by coefficient, separates diagonal and off-diagonal recurrences, identifies the formal exponent matrix as A^(r), and proves polynomial majorant bounds for the nonlinear recurrence using the leading-eigenvalue gap. The existing global small-exponent triangularization criterion in Theorem2.1 is expressly credited to [7,8] and is background; Section3 supplies the new coefficient-to-exponent control needed to apply it. The packet fixes all Poincare ranks and selects already diagonal leading matrices, exactly the normalization in which the author writes the recurrence, avoiding any additional uniform change-of-basis claim.

statement_scope: Theorem3.1 with the explicitly fixed singular locations a_i and positive Poincare ranks r_i, in the diagonal-leading slice of the compact nonresonant parameter set D. The rational p-by-p system on the Riemann sphere has the Laurent form (2.2), infinity nonsingular, each leading B_i^(0) diagonal with pairwise distinct eigenvalues and their gap bounded away from zero on the chosen compact set. For sufficiently small B_i^(1),...,B_i^(r_i), with the smallness threshold allowed to depend on these fixed ranks and gap, all solutions are Liouvillian iff every Laurent coefficient matrix is simultaneously upper triangular under one constant invertible conjugation. This selects a valid explicit subclass of the paper main theorem, whose proof starts by diagonalizing B^(0). No rank-uniform threshold, coalescing-leading-spectrum limit, Fuchsian extension, or different solvability-type corollary is asserted.
editorial_warning: The printed threshold notation delta(D,p,n) suppresses the already fixed Poincare ranks; the explicit proof majorant P_{r-1} depends on the rank, which is retained in the selected scope. The leading matrices are selected already diagonal so the author written norm estimates apply in that basis; no unsupplied uniform eigenbasis estimate is asserted. Previously published Theorem2.1 is credited background, not a separately counted proof.
